items.title: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching
items.desc: Purpose CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vulnerability CVE-2026-114938 . This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK). Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution. Actions to take CISA urges organizations to take the following actions: Identify affected Java installations. Review your software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances. Note: JDKs and Java runtimes may not appear as separate entries in software inventories. Apply relevant Java and vendor patches as soon as they are available, prioritizing internet-facing systems. If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access. Review Oracle’s security advisory for guidance on patching and affected products and versions. Monitor for indicators of suspicious activity, including rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes, and suspicious Java processes. items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.desc: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-114713 UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability CVE-2026-123039 Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

items.desc: Zoom a publié des correctifs pour deux vulnérabilités affectant Workplace sous Windows, dont une faille critique d’élévation de privilèges notée 9,6 sur l’échelle CVSS. Référencées CVE-2026-108186 et CVE-2026-108187, elles pourraient permettre à un attaquant non authentifié d’obtenir des privilèges supplémentaires à distance, à condition que l’utilisateur interagisse. Les entreprises sont invitées à déployer rapidement les mises à jour.

items.title: Grok Build : plus de 35 000 applications IA accessibles sans authentification
items.desc: Une étude de la société de cybersécurité Claroc révèle d’importants défauts de confidentialité dans des applications créées avec Grok Build, l’outil de création d’applications assistée par IA de SpaceXSI, l’éditeur de Grok anciennement appelé xAI. Sur les 37 571 applications actives examinées, 35 578 étaient accessibles sans authentification, exposant potentiellement des données personnelles, des documents internes et des identifiants sensibles.

items.title: Scality devient autorité de numérotation CVE sous l’égide de l’ENISA
items.desc: Scality a annoncé le 10 novembre 2026 son entrée dans le programme CVE en tant qu’autorité de numérotation, ou CNA (CVE Numbering Authority). L’éditeur peut désormais attribuer directement des identifiants aux vulnérabilités de ses logiciels et publier les enregistrements associés. Cette évolution intervient alors que les obligations de signalement du Cyber Resilience Act sont applicables depuis septembre.

items.title: Cisco et IBM vont intégrer Mythos à leurs outils de cybersécurité
items.desc: Cisco et IBM préparent l’intégration de Claude Mythos dans leurs produits de sécurité. Le premier utilisera le modèle d’Anthropic pour renforcer les tests offensifs des systèmes d’IA. Le second vise la détection et la correction de vulnérabilités logicielles. Ces projets élargissent l’accès aux capacités de Mythos, avec des conditions d’utilisation et des calendriers distincts.
